page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.metal-48xl is a compute-optimized bare-metal instance based on 64-bit Arm architecture. It features 192 physical AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 2.7 GHz without SMT, providing dedicated single-threaded core allocation. The server is equipped with 384 GB of DDR5 memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Direct-attached local storage includes 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD, and network throughput is configured with a 50 Gbps baseline capacity.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong multi-threaded compute density and high memory transfer rates. In stress-ng multi-core testing, the server achieves top-tier throughput alongside memory bandwidth exceeding 909 GB/sec read and 403 GB/sec write on large data blocks. Application-specific tests show top-tier metrics for PassMark database operations, Geekbench software compilation using Clang, static web serving throughput at 144.2 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations reaching 383.07 million operations per second. In contrast, single-threaded performance in Geekbench and stress-ng measures in the average performance tier.

The hardware configuration provides core density and fast local SSD storage without virtualization hypervisor overhead. A key trade-off appears in LLM text generation performance, where token output speed remains in the lower tiers across small, medium, and large model evaluations. The server fits high-concurrency database deployments, large software build pipelines, in-memory caching systems, static web serving, and parallel data processing jobs that utilize local storage and high core counts.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gd.metal-48xl is a compute-optimized bare-metal instance powered by 192 physical ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores running at 2.7 GHz. Equipped with 384 GB of DDR5 RAM (2 GB per core) and 11,400 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage, it offers a 50 Gbps baseline network capacity. In benchmarks, the server demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and software compilation speed, along with top-tier throughput in Redis SET operations and database tasks. However, single-threaded performance is in the average tier, and LLM text generation speeds are low. This instance provides scalable processing density for multi-threaded workloads, fitting high-throughput databases, software compilation, static web serving, and parallel data processing.
